Erlitou page: 'Preceded by: Longshan culture', 'Early estimates dated it from approximately 1900 to 1500 BC'; the Yueshi arose 'following the decline of the Longshan culture in the North China Plain' after a flood of about 1920 BC. Successors and their land in identity.successors.

notes: Written by g-ea (gap batch) on 2026-11-01 from three pages. Cliopatria has no Longshan row. The page gives provinces and site names, never a boundary, so the keyframes reuse the Yangshao and Dawenkou handover regions exactly as those dossiers hand them over; the Yangshao field (Wei valley, Shanxi, Henan, southern Hebei) is drawn as one culture although the page treats Henan, Hougang II, Taosi and Shaanxi as separate variants (Chang's 1963 'Longshanoid horizon' was later split into regional cultures). The -2000 loss and the central area are the researcher's reading (confidence 2). Taosi (southern Shanxi) is inside the 'central area' here although the page says Taosi shows no continuity with Erlitou. Successors erlitou-culture and yueshi-culture have no dossier (counterparts_needing_dossiers). Wikidata id left null: no page opened gives it.
